title: Stop arguing with what is already under Hukam
summary: Past actions cannot be rewritten, and tomorrow is not in the ego's possession. Mercy begins when regret stops prosecuting what the Doer already holds.
takeaway: Let regret stop litigating what the Doer already holds.
lifeApplication: When the mind reopens the old case, refuse the courtroom. Name the past plainly, ask for the Guru's teaching, and place the next step under trust.

source.shortMeaning: Past actions cannot be erased, and what pleases the Divine comes to pass without another Doer.
source.lifeApplication: When regret reopens, return the moment to Hukam before arguing again.

evidence.coreClaim: Past actions cannot be erased, and what pleases the Divine comes to pass without another Doer.
evidence.turn: Regret softens when the heart stops trying to become the judge of reality.
evidence.practicalImplication: When the mind reopens the old case, refuse the courtroom. Name the past plainly, ask for the Guru's teaching, and place the next step under trust.
